topics.name: Present perfect and present perfect continuous

options: We want to build a strong India.
We want to builds a strong India.
We want to building a strong India.
questions.rule: After to, use the base form (the infinitive): to build. It never takes -s or -ing.

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct tense.
options: India has been a free country for 1947.
India has been a free country since 1947.
India is a free country since 1947.
questions.rule: From a point in the past till now, use the present perfect with since + point of time: has been ... since 1947.

options: If we work hard, India will become a developed nation.
If we will work hard, India will become a developed nation.
If we work hard, India become a developed nation.
questions.rule: Type 1 conditional: If + simple present, will + base verb. No will in the if-part.

options: The new metro is not only fast but also cheaply.
The new metro is not only fast but also cheap.
The new metro is not only fast and also cheap.
questions.rule: not only pairs with but also, and both parts must match: two adjectives, fast and cheap.

options: Can you tell me where the ISRO office is?
Can you tell me where is the ISRO office?
Can you tell me where the ISRO office?
questions.rule: Inside a sentence, a wh-clause keeps statement order: where the ISRO office is.

options: Manish like to play football every evening.
Manish likes to play football every evening.
Manish likes to plays football every evening.
questions.rule: The finite verb agrees with Manish (likes); the non-finite to play never changes.

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct tense.
options: Our scientists has been working on this satellite for three years.
Our scientists have been worked on this satellite for three years.
Our scientists have been working on this satellite for three years.
questions.rule: Present perfect continuous = have/has been + -ing. Plural scientists take have.

options: If we were more self-reliant, we will not depend on imported goods.
If we were more self-reliant, we would not depend on imported goods.
If we are more self-reliant, we would not depend on imported goods.
questions.rule: Type 2 conditional (imagined): If + simple past, would + base verb.

chat: What do you want to be when you grow up?
options: I want to becomes a scientist.
I want to become a scientist.
questions.rule: want + to + base verb: want to become.

chat: How long have you been waiting here?
options: I am waiting for twenty minutes.
I have been wait for twenty minutes.
I have been waiting for twenty minutes.
questions.rule: Waiting from the past till now: have been + -ing + for + length of time.

chat: Will you come to the science exhibition tomorrow?
options: Yes, if I finish my homework, I will come.
Yes, if I will finish my homework, I come.
Yes, if I finished my homework, I will come.
questions.rule: Type 1: if + simple present (finish), then will + base verb (will come).

chat: Do you know why Dr Kalam is called the Missile Man?
options: Yes, ma'am. It is because of he led India's missile programme.
Yes, ma'am. It is because led India's missile programme.
Yes, ma'am. It is because he led India's missile programme.
questions.rule: because begins a clause (subject + verb). because of is followed by a noun phrase, not a clause.

chat: Is your new school bag good?
options: Yes, it is not only light but also strong.
Yes, it not only light but also strong.
Yes, it is not only light and also strong.
questions.rule: Keep the verb is, and pair not only with but also.

chat: Have you finished your project on Dr Kalam?
options: Not yet. I am working on it since Monday.
Not yet. I have been worked on it since Monday.
Not yet. I have been working on it since Monday.
questions.rule: Still working, starting Monday: present perfect continuous have been working ... since.

chat: Why did you go to the library?
options: I went there to borrow a book on satellites.
I went there to borrowed a book on satellites.
I went there for borrow a book on satellites.
questions.rule: Purpose is shown by the infinitive to + base verb: to borrow.

chat: What would you do if you were the Prime Minister?
options: If I was the Prime Minister, I will build more schools.
If I were the Prime Minister, I build more schools.
If I were the Prime Minister, I would build more schools.
questions.rule: Imagined situation (type 2): If I were ..., I would + base verb.

questions.prompt: Replace the phrase 'his place of birth' with a clause.
questions.source: Do you know his place of birth?
options: Do you know where was he born?
Do you know where he was born?
Do you know where he is born?
questions.rule: The clause where he was born has a subject and verb in statement order.

questions.source: If you do not practise, you will not improve.
options: Unless you do not practise, you will not improve.
Unless you practise, you will improve.
Unless you practise, you will not improve.
questions.rule: Unless means if not, so drop the not from the if-part only.

questions.source: Dr Kalam was a scientist. He was also a poet.
options: Dr Kalam was not only a scientist and also a poet.
Dr Kalam was not only a scientist but also a poet.
Dr Kalam were not only a scientist but also a poet.
questions.rule: Place not only and but also just before the two matching parts: a scientist / a poet.

questions.prompt: Combine into one sentence beginning with 'Having'.
questions.source: Kabir finished his homework. He went out to play.
options: Having finish his homework, Kabir went out to play.
Having finished his homework, Kabir went out to play.
Having finished his homework, went out to play.
questions.rule: Having + past participle shows the first action; the main clause still needs its subject, Kabir.

questions.source: Neha started learning the violin in 2022, and she is still learning it.
options: Neha has been learning the violin since 2022.
Neha is learning the violin since 2022.
Neha has been learnt the violin since 2022.
questions.rule: Started in the past and still going on: has been + -ing + since + starting point.

questions.prompt: Replace the phrase 'In his absence' with a clause.
questions.source: In his absence, the thieves looted his house.
options: While he away, the thieves looted his house.
While he was away, the thieves looted his house.
While was he away, the thieves looted his house.
questions.rule: A clause needs a subject and a verb in statement order: While he was away.

questions.source: We do not have enough satellites, so we cannot forecast every storm.
options: If we had enough satellites, we could forecast every storm.
If we have enough satellites, we could forecast every storm.
If we had enough satellites, we can forecast every storm.
questions.rule: An imagined present (type 2): If + simple past (had), then could + base verb.

questions.source: We must be strong as a military power and as an economic power.
options: We must be strong not only as a military power and also as an economic power.
We must not only be strong as a military power but also an economic power.
We must be strong not only as a military power but also as an economic power.
questions.rule: Pair not only with but also and keep both parts alike: as a military power / as an economic power.
